entry.title: Suggested Labels [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

The label picker now surfaces your most relevant labels at the top, so you can apply the right label in seconds instead of scrolling through hundreds of options. A "Suggested labels" group shows labels you've recently used alongside the most popular ones in the repo, each with a short reason so you always know why they appear. This makes labeling faster and more accurate, whether you're triaging a single issue or working through a backlog.

Expected Outcome

Developers and maintainers spend less time hunting for the right label and more time doing meaningful work, resulting in better-labeled issues and pull requests across the board. By reducing choice fatigue in repos with large label sets, teams can triage more consistently and keep their workflows moving. Over time, smarter label suggestions help contributors get onboarded faster and keep project organization healthy with less manual effort.

entry.title: Pinned Items — pin Projects, Views & Milestones to the sidebar [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Pinned Items lets you save up to 25 projects, views, and milestones directly in the repository sidebar, so your most-used destinations are always one click away. Whether you're tracking a milestone, jumping back to a saved issue query, or checking in on a project board, you get there without navigating through menus every time. Your sidebar becomes a persistent launchpad tailored to how you actually work.

Expected Outcome

Saved views are powerful, but only if people come back to them — and data from the preview showed that most users who created a view never returned to it. Pinned Items closes that gap by keeping the things you care about visible and reachable in the sidebar at all times. The goal is to make saved views, projects, and milestones a natural part of the daily workflow, not a feature people set up once and forget.

entry.title: Archive labels [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

You can now archive labels to retire them from active use without deleting them or losing any history. Archived labels disappear from pickers, autocomplete, and suggestions immediately, so your label list stays clean and relevant — while remaining applied to all existing issues, pull requests, and discussions. Un-archiving brings a label back at any time, so there's no risk in tidying up.

Expected Outcome

Repositories with long histories tend to accumulate hundreds of unused labels that clutter the label picker and slow down triage. Archive labels gives maintainers a safe, reversible way to retire labels they no longer need, so contributors can find the right labels quickly. The result is a cleaner labeling workflow and less friction when organizing and prioritizing work.

entry.title: Path-based exclusions for push rules in Rulesets [Public Preview] [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Path-based exclusions in push rulesets let you apply file push rules only where they matter — protecting critical paths while skipping generated code, documentation, or vendored assets that don't need the same governance. You get precise, surgical control over enforcement without loosening protections elsewhere in your repository. Exclusions are validated at setup time, so misconfigurations are caught before they reach your developers.

Expected Outcome

Teams can enforce strong push rules across their repositories without creating unnecessary friction for paths that follow different conventions. By giving admins the flexibility to exclude specific directories, this feature reduces workarounds, support requests, and the pressure to choose between blanket enforcement and blanket exemption. The result is a more accurate and trustworthy governance layer that reflects how real codebases are structured.

entry.title: GitHub Advanced Security trials on Team platform [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Team plan customers can now try GitHub Advanced Security with a self-serve trial before making a purchase decision. This gives Team customers hands-on access to security capabilities like code scanning, secret scanning, and dependency review to evaluate the real-world impact on their codebase. There's no commitment required to get started — just a direct path to understanding whether GitHub Advanced Security is right for your team.

Expected Outcome

Customers on the Team plan can now experience GitHub Advanced Security firsthand, removing the guesswork from the buying process. Teams can make confident, informed decisions about investing in advanced security tooling.

entry.title: Arbitrary issuers and claims for federated credentials [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

You can now authenticate GitHub Apps using any compatible identity provider — including SPIFFE, Okta, GCP, AWS, Kubernetes clusters, and more — instead of managing private keys. Configure any issuer and claims that fit your infrastructure, and use federated credentials to mint installation tokens for your app's installations. This gives every team, regardless of their technology stack, a secure and flexible alternative to long-lived private keys.

Expected Outcome

Developers and platform teams can eliminate the operational burden of storing, rotating, and securing GitHub App private keys by integrating directly with the identity providers already powering their infrastructure. By extending federated credential support to any compatible issuer, GitHub Apps fit naturally into modern zero-trust and cloud-native environments. The result is a more secure authentication model that reduces credential sprawl and scales with the diversity of real-world infrastructure setups.

entry.title: Allow users with triage role or higher to archive pull requests [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Users with the triage role (and above) can now archive pull requests, giving repository maintainers the flexibility to delegate PR hygiene to trusted moderators without granting them write access to code. This aligns pull request archiving with the intended scope of the triage role — handling moderation tasks that don't modify source code. Teams managing large or open source repositories can distribute cleanup work more effectively across their contributors.

Expected Outcome

By expanding archiving permissions to include triage, write, maintain, and admin roles, teams can reduce their reliance on write-level collaborators for routine PR housekeeping like closing spam or stale pull requests. This removes a friction point in open source and large-team workflows where trusted triagers were previously blocked from performing straightforward moderation tasks. The change brings the permission model in line with maintainer expectations and enables cleaner, faster PR management at scale.

entry.title: Public monitoring ability to dismiss/reopen alerts [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

You can now dismiss and reopen public monitoring alerts, with an optional comment explaining your decision. This makes it easier to triage large volumes of alerts and keep your security workflow organized. Teams can quickly mark resolved or irrelevant alerts as closed, so the active alert list stays focused on what actually needs attention.

Expected Outcome

Security teams working with high volumes of public monitoring alerts gain a faster, more structured way to manage their alert queues. By enabling dismissal and reopening with optional context, teams can reduce noise and make triage more consistent across contributors. The result is a cleaner, more actionable view of real security signals.

entry.title: OIDC EMU users can silently SSO into GitHub from the GH Copilot CLI without ever signing into GitHub [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Enterprise Managed Users on Windows can now sign in to the GitHub Copilot CLI using their existing Entra (Microsoft) account — no separate GitHub username, URL, or sign-in required. The CLI detects your Windows account and offers a one-tap sign-in experience that feels just like other Microsoft apps your team already uses. This removes a major onboarding hurdle for organizations adopting GitHub Copilot with Enterprise Managed Users.

Expected Outcome

Getting developers productive on GitHub Copilot should be fast and frictionless, not a support event. By enabling silent single sign-on through Entra for OIDC-based EMU organizations, GitHub reduces the time it takes for new users to go from install to working — and lowers the burden on IT admins fielding sign-in questions during migrations and enablement. This feature lays the foundation for broader seamless access across more identity providers, enterprise configurations, and applications over time.

entry.title: Add option to block users on personal accounts from comments or PRs [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

You can now block a user directly from a pull request or issue comment — no need to navigate away, visit a profile, or lose your place in the conversation. A streamlined modal lets you add an optional moderation note and confirm the action in just a few clicks, keeping your context intact. This makes it faster and less disruptive to handle spam and abuse right where it happens.

Expected Outcome

Maintainers who deal with high volumes of spam or disruptive contributors should be able to act quickly without the overhead of a multi-step, multi-page workflow. By surfacing the block action in context and supporting moderation notes, we want to make it easier to maintain a healthy, focused contribution environment at scale. The goal is to give maintainers more control over their projects without pulling them away from the work that matters.

entry.title: Ability to add a note explaining why user is bypassed from PR limits [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

When adding someone to a repository's pull request bypass list, maintainers can now include a note explaining the reason for the exception. This added context makes it easy for the whole team to understand why each bypass exists — even as the list grows over time. Keeping that history visible helps teams maintain cleaner, more auditable workflows without relying on memory or out-of-band communication.

Expected Outcome

As bypass lists scale across larger teams and repositories, the intent behind each entry can become unclear, creating confusion and governance gaps. This change gives maintainers a lightweight way to document decisions inline, improving transparency and reducing the overhead of managing access over time. Teams that rely on automated bypass additions will also benefit from automatically generated reasons, ensuring full visibility with no extra effort.

entry.title: Secret scanning detects secrets in Actions logs [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Secret scanning now detects secrets exposed in GitHub Actions workflow logs, closing a common and high-risk gap in your security coverage. When a token, API key, or credential surfaces in a log, GitHub will automatically open a secret scanning alert with additional information about the finding.

Expected Outcome

Development teams need confidence that their automation pipelines are covered alongside their source code and GitHub surfaces. By extending secret scanning to Actions logs, developers can ship faster without worrying that their pipelines are silently leaking credentials.

entry.title: Add ability to set PR limits at an org level [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

You can now set pull request limits across an entire organization from a single place, rather than configuring each repository individually. Org-level bypass lists let you manage trusted contributors centrally, so the right people always have access without repeating that work repo by repo. This makes it practical to enforce consistent contribution policies at scale, even across organizations with hundreds of repositories.

Expected Outcome

Teams managing large numbers of repositories gain meaningful time back by configuring PR limits once at the org level instead of touching every repo. Central bypass list management reduces the risk of inconsistent trust settings slipping through the cracks. The result is a more reliable and maintainable workflow for maintainers who need to govern open source or enterprise contribution policies at scale.

entry.title: Improving performance for scheduled workflows
entry.content:
Value Prop

Improved performance in how scheduled workflows are handled. Customers will experience more reliable execution of their scheduled workflows, with fewer workflows being dropped due to system load.

Expected Outcome

Improved performance for scheduled workflows and a significant reduction in the number of workflows delayed. Customers can rely on their scheduled workflows running consistently and on time.

entry.title: Add a setting that allows draft PRs to account towards a users limit [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Repository maintainers can now configure draft pull requests to count toward a user's pull request limit, closing a loophole that allowed contributors — or automated agents — to open unlimited draft pull requests. This gives teams stronger control over their contribution workflows, reducing unwanted noise from notifications, unnecessary CI runs, and a cluttered pull request list. Whether you're managing a large open source project or enforcing contribution policies in an enterprise environment, this setting helps your limits actually work as intended.

Expected Outcome

Teams that rely on pull request limits to manage spam or enforce contribution policies will have a more effective tool that covers both open and draft pull requests. By making this behavior configurable, maintainers can tailor the setting to their repository's needs without impacting teams who prefer the existing behavior.

entry.title: GitHub Actions Cache Isolation [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Cache Isolation for GitHub Actions gives users and organizations the ability to create secure, partitioned cache environments for their workflows. This feature helps prevent accidental or malicious data leaks between workflows, offering fine-grained control and audit capabilities for enterprise-grade automation.

Expected Outcome

By isolating caches by repository, workflow, or branch, this update aims to eliminate risks like cache poisoning and data exfiltration, improving the security and reliability of CI/CD pipelines. Customers can expect more trustworthy and predictable workflow runs, with enhanced control over how and when caches are accessed or modified.

entry.title: Actions Runner Controller Release 0.15.0 [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

With the Actions Runner Controller 0.14.1 release, platform teams and open source contributors can more easily manage self-hosted runners on Kubernetes. This update delivers quality-of-life improvements, clearer configuration, better troubleshooting, and incorporates valuable community contributions, making day-to-day operations smoother and more reliable.

Expected Outcome

We aim to reduce friction for teams operating and maintaining ARC by addressing community-reported issues and enhancing the developer experience. This release builds trust in the ARC release process and helps teams confidently migrate away from legacy solutions while benefiting from a more polished and stable platform.

entry.title: Scale Set Job To Runner Assignment [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

With Scale Set Job To Runner Assignment, customers using GitHub Actions Scale Sets can automatically distribute jobs to the most suitable runners, making large-scale CI/CD workflows faster and more efficient. This feature reduces wait times and resource waste by ensuring jobs are assigned where they can run best, even as demand changes.

Expected Outcome

We want customers to experience smoother, more reliable automation at scale, with less manual intervention and fewer workflow bottlenecks. By improving job placement and scheduling, this release aims to help teams deliver software faster and more predictably.

entry.title: Release: Elevate Attestation as a First-Class Object in Repository UI and Security Overview [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

You can now easily view and verify attestations directly in your repository’s UI and Security Overview, with clear SLSA level indicators. This makes it simpler for developers, security admins, and compliance leads to assess trust and compliance at a glance, streamlining your security workflows.

Expected Outcome

By making attestations a first-class part of the repository experience, we aim to reduce friction and increase adoption of secure development practices. This change helps enterprise teams meet SLSA source track requirements and strengthens trust in your software supply chain.

entry.title: SBOM Export user interface and API support retrieval of dependency snapshots [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub now lets you export and retrieve Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs,) including dependency snapshots, through both the UI and a fast, asynchronous API. Instead of generating SBOMs on demand (which was slow and subject to strict rate limits), SBOMs are now pre-stored for rapid retrieval, so you get reliable, consistent results even across large estates with tens of thousands of repositories. This makes it straightforward to integrate with third-party SCA tools, automate compliance reporting, and maintain internal audit records at scale.

Expected Outcome

Enterprise customers managing large codebases have been unable to programmatically traverse their full repository estate for SBOMs due to synchronous API limitations, aggressive rate limits, and no guarantee of a response for any given request. With this release, we resolve those pain points by delivering a redesigned backend that supports asynchronous retrieval of pre-built SBOMs, including artifact and snapshot-level granularity. The expected outcomes are: (1) customers can reliably export SBOMs at scale without hitting availability issues, (2) integration with external compliance and SCA tooling becomes seamless, and (3) GitHub strengthens its position as the default platform for end-to-end supply chain security.
